newsitem.title: USA: Chrysler long-term debt, pfd stock upgraded.
newsitem.headline: Chrysler long-term debt, pfd stock upgraded.

text.p: Duff & Phelps Credit Rating Co said it upgraded the long-term debt of Chrysler Corp to single-A from single-A-minus.
The credit rating firm said it also upgraded the automaker's preferred stock to single-A-minus from triple-B-plus.
Chrysler and its Chrysler Financial Corp financing unit had a total of $16 billion of debt outstanding on March 31, including about $3 billion of commercial paper, Duff & Phelps said.
"This upgrade is due mainly to increased confidence in Chrysler's ability to maintain its competitiveness, even in a potential economic recession," the firm said.

"Major keys include Chrysler's fine overall cost structure and its good design execution and product development nimbleness, which will enable it to respond quickly to changes in consumer tastes and market conditions," Duff & Phelps said.
"The upgrade considers the intensely competitive environment of the domestic auto industry, which may be further amplified by any major economic recession," it said.
